periods_or_stages.name: Johnson's scalar-stress model
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a. It applies whenever groups grow (PPNB mega-sites, Ubaid, Uruk).
periods_or_stages.defining_features: When a decision-making group grows past about 6 units, consensus stress rises. Groups respond either by nesting into a 'sequential' (egalitarian, consensus-based) hierarchy of bigger units, or by creating a 'simultaneous' institutional hierarchy of offices. Dispute frequency rises with communication stress.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: The trigger mechanism for G5. It can be modelled as a threshold that fires as soon as village or household numbers pass a limit, even in G2.
sources: Johnson, G. 1982. 'Organizational structure and scalar stress.' In Renfrew, Rowlands & Segraves (eds.), Theory and Explanation in Archaeology, 389-421. Bibliographic summary: https://mapaspects.org/biblio/ref_4260/index.html

periods_or_stages.name: Halstead's 'normal surplus'
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a. Built on Neolithic Thessaly, about 7th to 5th millennium BC.
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Overproduction is a normal hedge against bad years, not a sign of unusually good conditions. Most of the time the surplus is used up or shared, so it does not automatically feed specialists. How surplus turns into elites or non-producers is the problem to be explained.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Supports making G3 'surplus' an ordinary buffer from G2 onward, with specialists paid only when the surplus is large and dependable.
sources: Halstead, P. 1989. 'The economy has a normal surplus.' In Halstead & O'Shea (eds.), Bad Year Economics, 68-80: https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/bad-year-economics/economy-has-a-normal-surplus-economic-stability-and-social-change-among-early-farming-communities-of-thessaly-greece/D43A0CC496366ADDE55EB7CD507D8129

periods_or_stages.name: Childe's 10 urban criteria, mapped to phases
periods_or_stages.dates: Childe applied them to about 3,500 to 3,000 BC (Mesopotamia, Egypt, Indus)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: (1) Large, dense settlements. (2) Full-time specialists: craftsmen, transport workers, merchants, officials, priests. (3) Surplus paid as tithe or tax to a god or king. (4) Monumental public buildings. (5) A ruling class. (6) Writing and numbers, leading to exact sciences. (7) Elaborate art. (8) Long-distance trade. (9) Residence-based rather than kin-based community, held together by ideology. (10) The state.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: (1) G6; (2) G6 for full-time work, G3 for part-time; (3) G5-G6; (4) foreshadowed at Göbekli Tepe and Ubaid temples (G5), monumental in G6; (5) G5-G6; (6) G6, with tokens earlier; (7) throughout; (8) begins in G3 (obsidian, early pots), large-scale in G6; (9) G6; (10) G6. Childe's criteria therefore bundle G5 and G6, while part-time crafts and household property belong before them.
sources: Childe 1950 (as above)
Britannica on the urban revolution: https://www.britannica.com/print/article/619501
Smith, M.E. 2009. 'V. Gordon Childe and the Urban Revolution.' Town Planning Review 80(1):3-29, doi:10.3828/tpr.80.1.2a: https://d-meeus.be/biblio/Smith2009.html

major_breakpoints: Childe's original cut has two revolutions with a long, unnamed gap between them. The Neolithic Revolution covers food production, villages and population. The Urban Revolution covers cities, specialists, writing and the state, about 3,500 to 3,000 BC. Everything between about 6,500 and 4,000 BC (Late Neolithic and Chalcolithic: Hassuna, Halaf, Samarra, Ubaid) is that gap, and it is exactly where G3-G5 sit. (Childe 1936; Childe 1950, Town Planning Review 21:3-17)

Sedentism comes before farming. Natufian villages date from about 14,600 cal BP, and food storage before domestication appears at Dhra' about 11,300 cal BP. So 'village' (G1) and 'farming' (G2) are separate steps, and storage starts even before G2. (Bar-Yosef 1998; Kuijt & Finlayson 2009 PNAS)

Cultivation and herding begin about 11,500 cal BP, but domestic forms are only fixed about 10,500 to 10,000 cal BP (einkorn about 10,400 cal BP; Ganj Dareh goats about 10,000 cal BP). Scholars disagree over whether this took at least 1,000 years or 2,000-4,000 years (protracted model) or was faster (Abbo, Lev-Yadun & Gopher 2012). (Zeder 2011; Zeder & Hesse 2000; Fuller, Willcox & Allaby 2011; Asouti & Fuller 2013)

Neolithic Demographic Transition: fertility jumps when farming arrives locally, with a 500-700 year signal in Europe. It is dated relative to farming, so population growth belongs with G2, not only G1. (Bocquet-Appel 2011 Science; Bocquet-Appel 2011 Current Anthropology)

The PPNB mega-sites (10-14 ha) and their decline in the PPNC (about 8,900 to 8,600 cal BP, i.e. 6,950-6,650 cal BC) are the first 'scale crisis'. Large villages broke up rather than growing into towns. This is a natural break between an early-village block and a later block. (Kuijt 2000; Zielhofer et al. 2012; Rollefson)

Pottery begins about 7,000 to 6,700 cal BC in Upper Mesopotamia and about 6,400 BC in the southern Levant. That is roughly 2,500 years after cultivation began and before Ubaid, so pottery does not mark the Neolithic Revolution in the Near East. (Nieuwenhuyse ed. 2018; Yarmukian sources)

The Ubaid (about 6,500/6,200 to 3,800 BC) brings irrigation, temples, seals and chiefly households. This is where scholars place 'chiefdoms' (G5), even though burials show little elite display. (Stein 1994; Flannery 1999; Frangipane 2007)

Around 6,000 BP (about 4,000 BC) ox ploughs and land-limited farming go with a doubling of household-wealth Gini, part of Sherratt's 4th-millennium Secondary Products Revolution. This is a second, stronger inequality step, separate from early household storage. (Bogaard, Fochesato & Bowles 2019; Kohler et al. 2017; Sherratt 1981)

Towns come before writing. Tell Brak urban growth starts about 4,300 BC; Susiana settlement hierarchies form in Early to Late Uruk; complex tokens and bullae date about 3,700 to 3,500 BC. (Oates et al. 2007; Johnson 1973; Wright & Johnson 1975; Schmandt-Besserat 1996)

Late Uruk (about 3,500 to 3,100 BC) is the classic Urban Revolution: Uruk about 250 ha, numerical tablets about 3,500 to 3,350 BC, proto-cuneiform about 3,350 to 3,200 BC, Uruk expansion colonies. The network then collapsed around 3,000 BC. (Childe 1950; Algaze 1993/2005, 2008; Met Museum)
critiques_or_caveats: Childe's 10 criteria were taken from Mesopotamia itself, so applying them elsewhere amounts to comparing with Bronze Age Mesopotamia. They are not universal (Britannica; Roe 2014 https://joeroe.io/2014/01/27/not-so-civilised.html). Jason Ur argues Childe's 'city' is really a political form, and that the model does not even fit early Mesopotamian urbanism (https://jasonur.scholars.harvard.edu/publications/space-and-structure-early-mesopotamian-cities). Childe himself (1950) called the process gradual and cumulative, with intermediate stages.

The 'revolution' label hides how long these changes took. Protracted-domestication researchers say thousands of years; critics (Abbo, Lev-Yadun & Gopher 2012; Heun et al.) argue for a shorter window of about 1,200 years for einkorn. Fuller & Lucas (2025) find that sub-regional paths differ, so a single linear sequence is a simplification. https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10206457

G1-G6 are not strictly sequential in the evidence. Storage (G3-like) is found before domestication (PPNA), household-private storage (G4-like) in PPNB, scale problems (G5-like) at PPNB mega-sites, and plain tokens (G6-like) from about 8,000/7,500 BC. Many communities also kept an egalitarian ethos for a long time despite surplus (Çatalhöyük; Halaf). Reversals happened too: PPNC dispersal, and the Uruk collapse around 3,000 BC. Graeber & Wengrow (2021) push this further, though reviewers say they overgeneralise (https://www.historynewsnetwork.org/article/184781).

The dating of the Secondary Products Revolution is contested. Milk residues go back to the 7th millennium BC (Evershed 2008), plough marks at Sion to the early 5th millennium BC, and Greenfield (2010), Marciniak (2011) and Kristiansen & Sørensen (2020) say the model needs revising. Its importance may lie in large-scale adoption rather than first appearance.

House-size Gini (Kohler et al. 2017) is a proxy, and other variables can confound it. Bogaard et al. (2019) use 90 site-phases from 39 sites, and press figures differ. The 'ox-plough doubles Gini' claim is a statistical association across Western Eurasia, not a proven local mechanism.

Schmandt-Besserat's broad framework is widely accepted, but details are disputed: start dates for tokens (9,000-8,700, 8,000 or 7,500 BC), the meaning of individual token types, and the linear token-to-writing path. Some scholars also stress the influence of seal imagery (Kelley, Cartolano & Ferrara 2024, Antiquity).

Dates conflict between sources. Ubaid is given as 6,500-3,800 BC (Wikipedia) or 5,500-4,000 BC with origin about 6,200 BC (Met 2003). Uruk's size is given as 80, 100 or 250 ha, and population estimates (40,000-50,000) are modelled, not counted. Halaf is given as 6,100-5,100 BC or later. Cal BP and BC are often mixed up (cal BC ≈ cal BP minus 1,950); the conversions in this summary are mine.

The Levant-specific NDT dates are not verified. One southern Levant study using the NDT model found strong growth in Late Natufian, PPNA and PPNC but weaker growth in PPNB, which complicates a simple 'farming means a births boom' rule.

Johnson's 'about 6 units' threshold and the sequential/simultaneous distinction are taken from bibliographic summaries, not the full chapter. Kuijt (2000, and a 2025 lecture) warns that population estimates for Neolithic mega-sites are often inflated.
research.notes:
Proposed split for 'Society 2.0', based on where scholars draw the lines:

(A) 'Neolithic Revolution' block = G1 + G2, about 12,500 to 6,500 cal BC. This is Childe's single revolution, but later work separates it into Natufian sedentism, PPNA cultivation with storage, and PPNB domestication with the births boom. The PPNC dispersal around 6,950-6,650 BC is a natural closing event.

(B) Middle 'Late Neolithic / Chalcolithic' block = G3 + G4 + G5, about 7,000 to 4,000 BC. Childe gave this no name. Its internal cuts:
- pottery and part-time crafts from about 7,000 cal BC (G3);
- household storage, the first stage of property, about 7,000 to 5,000 BC (G4a; Çatalhöyük, Halaf/Samarra);
- Ubaid temples and chiefly households, about 6,200/5,500 to 4,000 BC (G5).

(C) 'Urban Revolution' block = G6, about 4,300 to 3,100 BC. Two optional sub-steps:
- proto-urban towns and complex tokens/bullae (Tell Brak about 4,300 BC; about 3,700 to 3,500 BC);
- Late Uruk city plus writing (about 3,500 to 3,100 BC).

Sherratt's Secondary Products Revolution and the ox-plough inequality jump (about 4,000 BC; the G4b stage) sit on the B/C boundary. Scholars treat that stronger inequality step as part of the run-up to urbanism, not part of early village property.

Specific adjustments for the phase anchors:
- G3 currently cites 'Ubaid' for the start of pottery. Pottery in the Near East starts about 7,000-6,700 cal BC (Pre-Proto-Hassuna, Sabi Abyad), and Ubaid fits G5 better.
- Childe's full-time specialists are an urban criterion (G6); part-time crafts belong in G3.
- Kohler 2017 and Varna (4,596-4,341 cal BC) both belong to the late, plough-linked G4b, not early household property.
- Simple tokens could be introduced as early as G2/G3. Complex tokens and bullae belong to late G5 / early G6.

Research limits: WebFetch to Wikipedia, metmuseum.org, PMC, utexas.edu, washington.edu and elsevierpure was blocked by the egress proxy. Most details therefore come from search-engine summaries of abstracts, publisher pages and secondary sources, not full texts. Kohler et al. 2017: I believe the title is 'Greater post-Neolithic wealth disparities in Eurasia than in North America and Mesoamerica' (Nature 551:619-622), but I could not confirm the exact title or pages. I could not confirm the claim that complex tokens appear about 4,400 BC; the sources I found put them in 3,500-3,100 BC, with envelopes from about 3,700 BC.

research.lens: Cross-regional comparison of the path from first farming villages to first cities and states with writing. Regions: China (Peiligang to Yangshao, Longshan, Erlitou and Shang), Egypt (Fayum/Merimde, Badarian, Naqada I-III, Dynasty 1), Mesoamerica (Archaic to Early, Middle and Late Formative, then Classic, with Oaxaca as the best-dated sequence) and Europe (LBK, Varna, Trypillia and the Aegean) as a contrast. The goal is to find breakpoints that recur across regions and to estimate how long each stage lasted, so the G1-G6 'Society 2.0' arc can be split into evidence-based sub-parts.

periods_or_stages.name: China 1: Early Neolithic villages (Peiligang / Cishan / Jiahu)
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 7000-5000 BCE (Peiligang; Columbia gives 6500-5000 BCE). Jiahu c. 7000-5800/5500 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Small sedentary villages with millet farming (rice at Jiahu), pigs and dogs. Pottery and kilns are present from the start. Jiahu: a moat enclosing about 5.5 ha, 45 houses, an estimated 250-800 people, and 300+ burials with uneven grave goods (bone flutes, turtle shells) that some read as early differentiation. More than 100 Peiligang sites are clustered in Henan.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G1+G2 together. In China pottery arrives with the first villages, so pottery is not a G3 (surplus and specialization) marker here.

periods_or_stages.name: China 2: Early Yangshao village communities
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 5000-4000 BCE (Yangshao overall c. 5000-3000 BCE; local radiocarbon sequences e.g. Shangluo c. 4200-2900 BCE)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Larger nucleated millet-farming villages. Liu (2004) dates the first clear social hierarchy only to mid-Yangshao, so this stage counts as growth without durable ranking.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G2-G3: intensified farming, population growth, household production. G4 not yet visible.
sources: Liu Li 2004, The Chinese Neolithic: Trajectories to Early States (CUP), excerpt: https://assets.cambridge.org/97805218/11842/excerpt/9780521811842_excerpt.htm
Columbia Early China presentation (as above)

periods_or_stages.name: China 3: Middle Yangshao / Miaodigou (first settlement hierarchy)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: In western Henan (Lingbao survey) there is rapid population growth, more sites and larger occupied areas, and the first settlement hierarchies. Very large public buildings appear (Xiahe F1 304.5 m2; Beiyangping c. 250 m2). Liu calls this the first clear evidence of social hierarchy, and archaeobotany ties it to intensive foxtail-millet agriculture.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Onset of G4+G5 together: ranking, a 2-tier settlement hierarchy and communal or elite buildings. Roughly equivalent to Ubaid-level chiefdoms.
sources: Liu Li 2004, chapter 'Reconstructing social processes' (mid-Yangshao c. 4000-3500 BC first clear hierarchy): https://resolve-he.cambridge.org/core/books/chinese-neolithic/reconstructing-social-processes/701446127039BDEDA15EC13E01BAD6CB

periods_or_stages.name: China 4: Late Neolithic regional polities (Liangzhu; Longshan walled towns, Taosi, Shimao)
periods_or_stages.dates: Liangzhu c. 3300-2300 BCE. Longshan c. 3000-1900 BCE (other sources 2800/2700-2000). Taosi c. 2300-1900 BCE. Shimao c. 2300-1800 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Liangzhu: a city site, a large water-control (dam) system, socially graded cemeteries with altars and jade (UNESCO calls it an 'early regional state'). Longshan: many rammed-earth walled towns. Taosi has a 280 ha enclosure with an inner wall separating elite from commoners and is often called an 'advanced chiefdom'. Shimao has stone walls with 4.2 and 5.7 km perimeters and about 80 sacrificed skulls under a gate. Large walled centres may have controlled up to about 2000 km2. Warfare, prestige goods and regional competition, but no writing.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Mature G5 plus the town part of G6 (regional centres, fortifications, prestige exchange) without the record part of G6. A good model for an intermediate 'competing chiefdoms' stage.

periods_or_stages.name: China 5: Erlitou (first urban state, no writing)
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 1750-1530 BCE (radiocarbon-based narrow range); older ranges c. 1900-1500 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Grew from a regional centre of about 100 ha (Phase I) to an urban site of about 300 ha (Phase II, c. 11,000 people) with a 12 ha palace zone bounded by roads, peaking near c. 24,000 people (Phase III). Large rammed-earth palace platforms and bronze ritual vessels. Widely treated as China's first state. The Xia identification is debated, and no writing has been found.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G6 town/state WITHOUT writing. In China the state comes before writing.
sources: Liu Li & Xu Hong 2007, 'Rethinking Erlitou: legend, history and Chinese archaeology', Antiquity 81: https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/rethinking-erlitou-legend-history-and-chinese-archaeology/FDBD0E8E7C661FC180CAD54AD9742E31

periods_or_stages.name: China 6: Late Shang oracle-bone writing
periods_or_stages.dates: Wu Ding reign radiocarbon-dated c. 1254-1197 BCE; Late Shang to c. 1046 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: The earliest attested full Chinese writing: divination records on bone and shell at Anyang (Yinxu), with 4,500+ distinct characters. This is about 500 years after Erlitou's urban state.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: The 'records' part of G6, arriving late. In China, writing and state formation are separate breakpoints.
sources: Oracle bone script (Wikipedia, citing AMS dating of inscribed bones): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_bone_script

periods_or_stages.name: Egypt 1: Neolithic (Fayum, Merimde Beni Salama)
periods_or_stages.dates: First domesticates in the Fayum c. 5400 BCE. Fayum Neolithic recalibrated c. 5700-4200 cal BCE (Kom K/W assemblages 4850-4250 BCE). Merimde c. 4800-4300 BCE (a radiocarbon start of c. 5300 BCE has been proposed)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: A Levantine package of wheat, barley, sheep and goat arrives ready-made, about 3,000 years after the Levantine PPNB. Fish remain a major food. Sites are only partly sedentary.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G1+G2 compressed because the package was imported rather than domesticated locally.
sources: Linseele et al. 2014 PLOS ONE (Fayum fauna, first domesticates): https://escholarship.org/content/qt76t2b2zs/qt76t2b2zs.pdf
Merimde culture (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merimde_culture
Wengrow 2006, The Archaeology of Early Egypt, 10,000-2,650 BC (CUP), table of contents: https://assets.cambridge.org/97805218/35862/toc/9780521835862_toc.pdf

periods_or_stages.name: Egypt 2: Badarian
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 4400-3800 BCE (table based on Dee et al. 2013); c. 4400-4000 BCE in older radiocarbon summaries
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Farming and herding communities in Upper Egypt with cemeteries and modest differences in grave goods. It overlaps with the earliest Naqada.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G2-G3: an established farming village society, early craft quality, little durable inequality.
sources: Dee et al. 2013, Proc. R. Soc. A 469: 20130395, 'An absolute chronology for early Egypt using radiocarbon dating and Bayesian statistical modelling': https://abdn.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/an-absolute-chronology-for-early-egypt-using-radiocarbon-dating-a
Stevenson 2016, 'The Egyptian Predynastic and State Formation', J. Archaeol. Res.: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10814-016-9094-7

periods_or_stages.name: Egypt 3: Naqada IA-IIB (local centres, elite cemeteries)
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 3800/3750-3450 BCE (Dee et al. 2013 model: Naqada starts c. 3800-3700 BCE, later than the old c. 4000 BCE)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Local centres at Hierakonpolis, Naqada and Abydos. Hierakonpolis HK6 is an elite cemetery (Tomb 23, Naqada IIA-B, 5.5 x 3.1 m, the largest of its date, with possible human and animal sacrifices), while HK43 is a 'working-class' cemetery with very few grave goods. Craft specialization in pottery, stone vessels and maceheads.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G3, G4 and G5 in quick succession, within a few centuries.
sources: Dee et al. 2013 (as above); Oxford news release: https://www.ox.ac.uk/node/11592
Hierakonpolis Expedition, predynastic cemeteries: https://hierakonpolis-online.org/index.php/explore-the-predynastic-cemeteries
Naqada culture (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naqada_culture

periods_or_stages.name: Egypt 4: Naqada IIC-IIIA (expansion, proto-kingdoms, first writing)
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 3450-3200 BCE (Dee et al. models make IIC-D much shorter than older chronologies; Hendrickx gives IIC-IID2 c. 3600-3350). Abydos tomb U-j (Naqada IIIA2) is dated c. 3320-3150 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Naqada material culture spreads north, and painted elite tombs appear (Hierakonpolis Tomb 100, Naqada IIC). Competing proto-kingdoms emerge. Tomb U-j holds about 150 inscribed bone and ivory labels, ink-inscribed jars and sealings: the earliest Egyptian writing, already using rebus phonograms.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Late G5 to early G6. Administrative records appear just before full territorial unification.
sources: Görsdorf, Dreyer & Hartung 1998, radiocarbon dates from Abydos cemetery U, Radiocarbon: https://journals.uair.arizona.edu/index.php/radiocarbon/article/download/3738/3163
Dee et al. 2014, 'Radiocarbon dating and the Naqada relative chronology', JAS 46: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0305440314000983

periods_or_stages.name: Egypt 5: Naqada IIIB-C / Dynasty 0-1 (territorial state)
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 3200-3000 BCE. Aha's accession modelled at 3111-3045 BCE (68% probability)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Named kings, unification of Upper and Lower Egypt, a royal cemetery at Abydos, and a bureaucracy using writing. Dee et al. describe the move from farming society to territorial state as faster than previously assumed.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Full G6: town or capital, records, territorial state. From first farming (c. 5400 BCE) to the state takes about 2,000-2,300 years, the shortest of the regions compared.
sources: Dee et al. 2013 (as above); PMC full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3780825/

periods_or_stages.name: Mesoamerica 1: Archaic (incipient cultivation before villages)
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 8000-2000 BCE (scheme-dependent). Maize domesticated in the Balsas about 9,000 years ago (c. 7000 BCE). Maize about 30% of diet c. 4700-4000 cal BP and a staple (over 70%) after c. 4000 cal BP (c. 2000 BCE)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Mobile or seasonal foragers-cultivators. Squash and maize were domesticated thousands of years before permanent villages. In Oaxaca, Gheo-Shih has an Archaic 'dance ground' dated 7720-7560 cal BC.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G2 BEFORE G1: cultivation precedes sedentism by about 5,000 years. This contradicts the Levantine G1-then-G2 order.
sources: Kennett et al. 2020 Science Advances, 'Early isotopic evidence for maize as a staple grain in the Americas' (UCSB release): https://news.ucsb.edu/2020/019919/roots-staple-crop
Marcus & Flannery 2004 FAMSI report (Gheo-Shih date, Tierras Largas men's houses): https://www.famsi.org/reports/03006/index.html
Mesoamerican chronology (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoamerican_chronology

periods_or_stages.name: Mesoamerica 2: Initial / Early Formative villages (Mokaya; Oaxaca Tierras Largas)
periods_or_stages.dates: Initial Formative c. 2000/1900-1200 BCE. Chiapas ceramic villages by c. 1550 BCE. Paso de la Amada occupied c. 1800-1000 BCE (ballcourt c. 1650-1400 BCE). Oaxaca Tierras Largas phase 1500/1400-1150 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: The first permanent villages arrive together with pottery. In Oaxaca, men's houses point to achievement-based (non-hereditary) leadership. Paso de la Amada has an 80 m ballcourt attached to high-status houses and a rich child burial, early signs of rank. Obsidian exchange is present from the beginning.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G1+G3 compressed: village, pottery, and exchange networks (part of G6) arrive almost at once. Early achievement-based leadership is a precursor to G5.
sources: Marcus & Flannery 2004 FAMSI (Tierras Largas 1500-1150 BC): https://www.famsi.org/reports/03006/index.html
Hill, Blake & Clark 1998 Nature 392, ballcourt at Paso de la Amada: https://ideas.repec.org/a/nat/nature/v392y1998i6679d10.1038_31837.html
Seshat, Oaxaca Tierras Largas (1400-1150 BCE): https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/523
UCSD Mesoamerican chronology outline: https://pages.ucsd.edu/~dkjordan/arch/mexchron.html

periods_or_stages.name: Mesoamerica 3: Early Formative chiefdoms (San Lorenzo Olmec; Oaxaca San José phase)
periods_or_stages.dates: San Lorenzo c. 1400-1000 cal BCE (peak 1200-1000). Oaxaca San José phase 1150-850 BCE, Guadalupe 850-700 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: San Lorenzo is a centre of about 775 ha with colossal heads, thrones and a multi-tier settlement system. Whether it was a chiefdom or a state is debated. In Oaxaca, San José Mogote grows in population and public buildings, with hereditary rank, craft areas and interregional exchange.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G4+G5 (hereditary rank and a regional centre) only about 300-400 years after the first villages.
sources: San Lorenzo Tenochtitlan (Wikipedia; Hirth & Cyphers 2020 dating): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Lorenzo_Tenochtitl%C3%A1n
Seshat, Oaxaca San José/Guadalupe phases: https://seshat-db.com/core/polity/523
Flannery & Marcus 2012, The Creation of Inequality (review): https://www.midwestarchaeology.org/sites/default/files/2013-BR16-Flannery-Marcus.pdf

periods_or_stages.name: Mesoamerica 4: Late Middle Formative competing chiefdoms (Oaxaca Rosario; La Venta)
periods_or_stages.dates: Rosario phase c. 700-500 BCE. La Venta c. 900-400 BCE. San José Mogote Monument 3 deposited no later than c. 650-560 BCE per Flannery & Marcus 2003 (contested)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Three chiefly polities, one in each arm of the Oaxaca Valley, separated by a buffer zone, with raiding and temple burning. Monument 3 shows a sacrificed captive with a calendrical name, one of the earliest Mesoamerican hieroglyphic texts.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Mature G5 (warfare, competing polities) plus the beginning of G6 records BEFORE the state. Glyphs come before the state here, the reverse of China.
sources: Flannery & Marcus 2003, 'The origin of war: New 14C dates from ancient Mexico', PNAS 100: 11801-11805: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1934526100
Univ. of Michigan Oaxaca archaeology, Origins of hieroglyphic writing: https://sites.lsa.umich.edu/oaxaca-archaeology/origins-of-hieroglyphic-writing-2/

Spencer & Redmond, Modeling expansionism and resistance: state formation in ancient Oaxaca: https://sociostudies.org/almanac/articles/modeling_expansionism_and_resistance_state_formation_in_ancient_oaxaca_mexico

periods_or_stages.name: Mesoamerica 5: Late Formative state formation (Monte Albán; early Maya writing)
periods_or_stages.dates: Monte Albán founded c. 500 BCE (Early MA I 500-300 BCE). State institutions in Late MA I, 300-100 BCE. Late/Terminal Formative c. 300 BCE-250 CE. San Bartolo Maya writing 300-200 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Population moves to a new hilltop capital (about 5,200 by 400 BCE and 17,200 by 200 BCE). A royal palace and multi-room temple appear together with conquest of regions more than a day's travel away (Spencer 2010: state institutions and territorial expansion coincide). Maya script and the 260-day calendar ('7 Deer') date to 300-200 BCE.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Full G6: a town or capital, state administration, writing. About 1,200-1,300 years after the first Oaxaca villages, but about 6,700 years after maize domestication.
sources: Spencer 2010, 'Territorial expansion and primary state formation', PNAS 107: 7119-7126: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2867764
Monte Albán (Wikipedia, citing Marcus & Flannery 1996): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Alb%C3%A1n
Science News on Saturno et al. 2006 (San Bartolo): https://www.sciencenews.org/article/getting-read-early-maya-writing
Mesoweb summary: https://www.mesoweb.org/reports/SanBartoloWriting.html

periods_or_stages.name: Mesoamerica 6: Classic
periods_or_stages.dates: c. 250-900 CE (Early Classic 250-600, Late Classic 600-900)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Mature city-states and large urban centres (Teotihuacan, Maya cities, Monte Albán), with full writing and dynastic monuments.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Beyond G6. This is the reference end point for a later 'Society 3.0'.
sources: Mesoamerican chronology (Wikipedia; Evans 2012 subdivisions): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoamerican_chronology

periods_or_stages.name: Europe 1: Early Neolithic of the Aegean and SE Europe
periods_or_stages.dates: Knossos (Crete) settled c. 7000 BCE, refined by Bayesian 14C to include an earlier aceramic phase
periods_or_stages.defining_features: A founding group of about 25-50 people with an imported Anatolian/Near Eastern farming package, wattle-and-daub huts, and burials under floors.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G1+G2 together (imported package).
sources: Douka et al. 2017 Antiquity, 'Dating Knossos and the arrival of the earliest Neolithic in the southern Aegean': https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/F4EEDD8990178B742BCD339CB8ABD02E
Knossos (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knossos

periods_or_stages.name: Europe 2: LBK first farmers of central Europe, and the Neolithic boom-bust
periods_or_stages.dates: LBK c. 5500 cal BCE to soon after 5000 cal BCE. Boom-bust cycles across c. 8000-4000 cal BP
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Longhouse villages, rapid expansion, denser settlement and regional pottery styles, ending with signs of stress or local crisis. Shennan et al. 2013: in 10 of 12 regions, populations rose 3-4 times after farming arrived and then fell by up to 60%, with no clear climate link, possibly from internal causes.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G1-G3 followed by collapse or reset rather than progress to G4-G6. Shows that 'stalled' or 'collapsed' should be valid simulation outcomes.
sources: Bickle & Whittle (eds) 2013, The First Farmers of Central Europe: Diversity in LBK Lifeways: https://www.bokus.com/bok/9781842179123/the-first-farmers-of-central-europe
Shennan et al. 2013 Nature Communications 4: 2486, 'Regional population collapse followed initial agriculture booms in mid-Holocene Europe': https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/1398968/
UCL news release: https://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/2013/oct/population-boom-and-bust-followed-start-farming-western-europe

periods_or_stages.name: Europe 3: Copper Age 'precocious' inequality (Varna)
periods_or_stages.dates: Varna cemetery modelled start 4596-4516 cal BCE, end 4427-4341 cal BCE (use span about 120-260 years)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Over 3,000 objects and more than 6 kg of gold, mostly in a few graves. Read as paramount chiefs or a strongly hierarchical society, though some argue for an early state and others for a less hierarchical order. It did not lead on to a state or writing.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G4+G5 reached without G6. An example of a dead end or reversal.
sources: Higham et al. 2007 Antiquity, 'New perspectives on the Varna cemetery': https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/new-perspectives-on-the-varna-cemetery-bulgaria-ams-dates-and-social-implications/0D02E895D9732774C4ED192C4D199417

Higham et al. 2018 Radiocarbon, 'AMS dating of the Late Copper Age Varna cemetery': https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/radiocarbon/article/ams-dating-of-the-late-copper-age-varna-cemetery-bulgaria/706A7F638D010BB6C943FBDFC1062749

periods_or_stages.name: Europe 4: Trypillia megasites (low-density urbanism without a state)
periods_or_stages.dates: Megasites of 100 ha or more c. 4100-3400 BCE. Maidanetske occupied c. 3990-3640 cal BCE. Talianki c. 3700-3600 BCE
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Settlements of up to 320 ha with about 2,300-3,000 houses and population estimates of 12,000-46,000 (depending on whether houses were occupied at the same time). Assembly houses but no palaces, royal tombs or writing. The sites later dispersed.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G6-sized settlements without G5/G6 institutions. Settlement size alone does not produce a state.
sources: Gaydarska et al., 'Trypillia megasites in context: independent urban development in Chalcolithic Eastern Europe', Cambridge Archaeological Journal: https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0959774319000301/type/journal_article
Müller et al., Maidanets'ke (Sidestone): https://www.sidestone.com/books/maidanets-ke
Settlements of the Cucuteni-Trypillia culture (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Settlements_of_the_Cucuteni%E2%80%93Trypillia_culture

periods_or_stages.name: Europe 5: Aegean palace states (Minoan Protopalatial)
periods_or_stages.dates: First palaces c. 1900 BCE (some say 2000 BCE). Cretan hieroglyphic in syllabic form by c. 1900 BCE, then Linear A
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Palaces at Knossos, Phaistos and Malia served as religious and administrative centres with storage. Clay accounting documents and seals. This was a secondary state formation in contact with Egypt and the Near East, about 5,000 years after first farming at Knossos.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G6 reached through contact (secondary), not independently.
sources: Knossos (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knossos
World History Encyclopedia, Linear A: https://worldhistory.org/Linear_A

periods_or_stages.name: Cross-regional stage A: Farming-village formation
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a (Levant PPNA-PPNB c. 9600-6500 BCE; China c. 7000-5000 BCE; Egypt c. 5400-4400 BCE; Oaxaca/Soconusco c. 1900-1150 BCE; central Europe 5500-5000 BCE)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Sedentary villages that depend on domesticates. Where the package was imported (Egypt, Europe) or co-developed (China), villages and farming appear together. Where crops were domesticated slowly (Mesoamerica), cultivation comes about 5,000 years before villages. Pottery usually arrives with the villages, except in the aceramic Levant.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G1+G2. In most regions these two are one breakpoint, not two.
sources: Kennett et al. 2020 (UCSB): https://news.ucsb.edu/2020/019919/roots-staple-crop
Linseele et al. 2014: https://escholarship.org/content/qt76t2b2zs/qt76t2b2zs.pdf
Bandy & Fox (eds) 2010, Becoming Villagers: Comparing Early Village Societies: https://uapress.arizona.edu/book/becoming-villagers

periods_or_stages.name: Cross-regional stage B: Growing village society (relatively egalitarian, achievement-based leaders)
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a. Lasts about 300 years (Oaxaca) to about 2,000-3,000 years (China, Levant PPNB to Halaf)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Population growth, village fissioning, household storage, part-time crafts, and non-hereditary leaders such as men's houses and big-men. Durable wealth inequality is still low. Kohler et al. 2025 find that persistent wealth inequality usually appears more than 1,000 years after cultivation begins.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G3 plus an early 'achieved leadership / dispute settlement' part taken out of G5.
sources: Flannery & Marcus 2012, The Creation of Inequality (three transitions: egalitarian to achievement-based to hereditary rank to state): https://www.midwestarchaeology.org/sites/default/files/2013-BR16-Flannery-Marcus.pdf
Kohler, Bogaard et al. 2025 PNAS (WSU release): https://news.wsu.edu/press-release/2025/04/15/new-study-reveals-wealth-inequalitys-deep-roots-in-human-prehistory/

periods_or_stages.name: Cross-regional stage C: Ranked society / simple chiefdoms (2-tier settlement hierarchy)
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a (China c. 4000-3500 BCE; Egypt c. 3750-3450 BCE; Oaxaca 1150-850 BCE; SE Europe Varna c. 4600-4350 BCE)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Hereditary rank, rich burials, a regional centre with satellite villages (one level of control above the village), public buildings, and prestige exchange. Wealth inequality and political hierarchy appear together and are linked to land becoming the limiting resource.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G4 + hereditary G5, best handled as one stage.
sources: Liu 2004 (mid-Yangshao hierarchy): https://resolve-he.cambridge.org/core/books/chinese-neolithic/reconstructing-social-processes/701446127039BDEDA15EC13E01BAD6CB
Kohler et al. 2017 Nature 551: 619-622 (house-size Gini): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5714260
Hierakonpolis HK6 elite cemetery: https://hierakonpolis-online.org/index.php/explore-the-predynastic-cemeteries

periods_or_stages.name: Cross-regional stage D: Competing complex chiefdoms / regional centres (3-tier)
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a (China Longshan/Liangzhu c. 3300-1900 BCE; Egypt Naqada IIC-IIIA c. 3450-3200 BCE; Oaxaca Rosario 700-500 BCE; Mesopotamia Late Ubaid to Early Uruk)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: Several rival polities, fortifications and buffer zones, raiding, monumental centres, regional styles, emblems and proto-writing such as seals, glyphs and tokens. Often unstable, with cycling between larger and smaller polities.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: Mature G5 plus the exchange and town parts of G6. This is the missing middle step between G5 and G6.
sources: Flannery & Marcus 2003 PNAS (Rosario warfare): https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1934526100
UNESCO Liangzhu: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1592
Taosi (Wikipedia): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taosi

periods_or_stages.name: Cross-regional stage E: Early state and town (4-tier hierarchy, bureaucracy), with or without writing
periods_or_stages.dates: n/a (Mesopotamia Uruk c. 3500-3100 BCE; Egypt c. 3200-3050 BCE; China Erlitou c. 1750-1530 BCE; Oaxaca 300-100 BCE)
periods_or_stages.defining_features: A capital town, palace and temple administration, three or more levels of decision-making above the village, and territorial expansion beyond one day's travel. Writing appears close to this stage but its timing varies: before the state in Oaxaca, together with it in Egypt, after it in China.
periods_or_stages.maps_to_phases: G6, which is better split into G6a (town/state) and G6b (records/writing) as separate triggers.
sources: Spencer 2010 PNAS: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2867764

Wright & Johnson 1975, 'Population, exchange, and early state formation in southwestern Iran', American Anthropologist 77: https://acawiki.org/Population,_Exchange,_and_Early_State_Formation_in_Southwestern_Iran
Shin et al. 2020 Nature Communications 11: 2394, 'Scale and information-processing thresholds in Holocene social evolution': https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7224170/

major_breakpoints: BP1, farming village established (G1+G2 merged): Levant c. 9600-8500 BCE; China c. 7000 BCE (Peiligang/Jiahu); Egypt c. 5400-5000 BCE (Fayum, Merimde); Soconusco/Oaxaca c. 1900-1400 BCE; central Europe c. 5500 BCE (LBK). The lag from domestication to village life varies a lot: about 5,000 years in Mesoamerica (maize c. 7000 BCE, staple only after c. 2000 BCE; Kennett et al. 2020, https://news.ucsb.edu/2020/019919/roots-staple-crop) but almost none where the package was imported (Egypt, Europe).

BP2, first durable inequality plus a 2-tier settlement hierarchy (G4 with hereditary G5): China mid-Yangshao c. 4000-3500 BCE (Liu 2004; Ma 2005), about 3,000 years after the first villages. Egypt Naqada I-IIB c. 3750-3450 BCE, about 1,600 years after the Fayum. Oaxaca San José phase 1150-850 BCE, only about 300 years after Tierras Largas. SE Europe Varna c. 4600 BCE. Kohler, Bogaard et al. 2025 PNAS (over 1,100 sites, about 47,000 houses): persistent wealth inequality generally lags the start of cultivation by more than 1,000 years and tracks land-limited production and settlement hierarchy (https://news.wsu.edu/press-release/2025/04/15/new-study-reveals-wealth-inequalitys-deep-roots-in-human-prehistory/).

BP3, competing complex chiefdoms / walled or monumental regional centres (the missing step between G5 and G6): China Liangzhu 3300-2300 BCE and Longshan 3000-1900 BCE (Taosi, Shimao); Egypt Naqada IIC-IIIA c. 3450-3200 BCE; Oaxaca Rosario 700-500 BCE (three polities, buffer zone, raiding; Flannery & Marcus 2003 PNAS). In most regions this stage lasts about 250-1,500 years and is where proto-writing and emblems appear.

BP4, state threshold (G6a): Spencer 2010 PNAS finds that bureaucratic state institutions and territorial expansion beyond one day's round trip appear together in Oaxaca (Late Monte Albán I, 300-100 BCE), Egypt, Mesopotamia (Uruk c. 3500 BCE onward), Peru and others (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2867764). Egypt reaches this point with Aha c. 3111-3045 BCE (Dee et al. 2013) and China with Erlitou c. 1750-1530 BCE. Archaeologically it is marked by three or more decision levels and a 4-tier settlement hierarchy (Wright 1977; Johnson 1982; see Wright & Johnson 1975).

BP5, information threshold (G6b, writing or records), which does NOT line up with BP4 across regions: Oaxaca glyphs c. 600 BCE come BEFORE the state (c. 300 BCE). In Egypt, Abydos U-j labels (c. 3320-3150 BCE) come together with unification (c. 3100). In China, oracle bones (c. 1250 BCE) come about 500 years AFTER Erlitou. Shin et al. 2020 (Seshat) model a 'scale threshold' after which polities invest in information processing, followed by an 'information threshold' that allows further growth (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7224170/).

Overall durations, village to state: Oaxaca about 1,200-1,300 years (but about 6,700 years from maize domestication); Egypt about 2,000-2,300 years from first domesticates; China about 5,000+ years (Peiligang to Erlitou); Levant/Mesopotamia about 6,000+ years (PPNA to Uruk, derived from the simulation's own anchors); Crete about 5,000 years to the palaces; central Europe had no pristine state. Borcan, Olsson & Putterman 2021 (Explorations in Economic History 82) estimate an average agriculture-to-state lag of about 3.1 millennia for internally originated states (https://ueaeprints.uea.ac.uk/id/eprint/80065).

Pattern in the durations: the early village era (BP1 to BP2) is the longest part almost everywhere. Once ranking appears, BP2 to BP4 tends to take only about 500-1,500 years, and in Egypt about 650 years. A simulation that spends equal time on G1-G6 will misrepresent the real tempo.
critiques_or_caveats: Unilinear stage schemes (band-tribe-chiefdom-state; Service/Fried) are widely criticized. Liu (2004) concludes that Chinese social change followed 'no pre-determined sequence', and Flannery & Marcus (2012) present the transitions as deliberate social manipulation, not automatic results of surplus or population. Treat the stages as recurring configurations, not a required ladder.

Sequence order differs by region. In Mesoamerica cultivation (G2) came about 5,000 years before villages (G1). In Egypt and Europe G1 and G2 arrived together as an imported package. Pottery (currently a G3 marker) appears with or before the first villages in China, Mesoamerica, Egypt and Europe, so it is a poor marker of surplus specialization outside the aceramic Levant.

Exchange is not a late stage. Obsidian and shell exchange is present from the first villages (e.g. Early Formative Oaxaca and Soconusco), and Wright & Johnson (1975) found inter-regional exchange insufficient on its own to explain state formation. Model exchange as a continuous variable from G1 onward rather than as part of G6 only.

G4 (property and inequality) and G5 (leaders) are not cleanly sequential. Achievement-based leaders such as men's houses (Tierras Largas, 1500-1150 BCE) come BEFORE hereditary inequality, while hereditary rank and wealth inequality appear TOGETHER with settlement hierarchy (Kohler et al. 2025). A better split is 'achieved leadership / dispute settlement' (early) versus 'hereditary rank plus property' (later, as one stage).

Writing and the state are separate breakpoints (state before writing in China, writing before state in Oaxaca, roughly simultaneous in Egypt). G6 should probably have independent triggers for 'town/state' and 'records'.

Reversibility is the norm. European examples include LBK boom-bust (Shennan et al. 2013), Varna wealth with no state, and the Trypillia megasites dispersing. Liangzhu ended around 2300 BCE. Chiefdoms are known to cycle. Shin et al. (2020) suggest polities below the information threshold are prone to collapse without obvious external causes. The simulation should allow stalls and regressions.

Chronological uncertainty: Naqada phase dates are reliable for the main blocks but not for individual phases (Dee et al. 2014). Longshan's start is given as 3000, 2800 or 2700 BCE depending on the source. Erlitou is given as 1750-1530 or 1900-1500 BCE. Oaxaca phase boundaries shift by about 100 years between Marcus & Flannery, Blanton et al. and Seshat. Monument 3 is dated anywhere from c. 650 BCE to after 200 BCE. Some popular figures mix calibrated and uncalibrated dates.

Contested classifications: Liangzhu is called an 'early regional state' by UNESCO but a complex chiefdom by others. San Lorenzo is debated between chiefdom and state. Erlitou's identification with Xia is debated and its state status is mainstream but not universal. Varna is read variously as chiefdom, early state or non-hierarchical. Trypillia populations (12,000-46,000) depend on assuming the houses were contemporary.
Summed-radiocarbon population proxies such as Shennan et al. 2013 are debated, because site counts can reflect research intensity and preservation as well as population.

Source-access limitation: WebFetch was blocked for most domains (PMC, Wikipedia, UCL, Royal Society), so many figures (e.g. Dee et al. 2013 phase dates, Erlitou populations, the Kohler 2025 numbers) come from abstracts, press releases or secondary summaries found by web search, not checked against full texts. The Badarian 4400-3800 BCE and Naqada IA-B 3750(?)-3650 BCE figures come from a summary table 'based on Dee et al. 2013' (likely Stevenson 2016), not the original paper.
research.notes:
PROPOSED SPLIT OF 'SOCIETY 2.0' BASED ON THE CROSS-REGIONAL EVIDENCE (for discussion with the user):

- 2.1 'Village formation' = G1+G2. Usually one breakpoint. Real duration from about 0 (imported package) to several thousand years.
- 2.2 'Growing village and crafts' = G3 plus achievement-based leaders and dispute settlement (an early, non-hereditary part of G5, e.g. men's houses or council). Often the longest stage: about 300 years (Oaxaca) to about 3,000 years (China).
- 2.3 'Ranked society' = G4 plus hereditary leaders, with a 2-tier settlement hierarchy (one centre and its satellites). Evidence: mid-Yangshao, Naqada I-IIB (Hierakonpolis), San José phase, Varna. About 300-600 years.
- 2.4 'Competing chiefdoms / regional centres' = a new intermediate stage. Several polities, walls or buffer zones, raiding, prestige exchange, seals, tokens and emblems, 3-tier hierarchy. Evidence: Longshan/Liangzhu, Naqada IIC-IIIA, Rosario, Late Ubaid to Early Uruk. About 250-1,500 years, with failure possible (Europe).
- 2.5 'Early state and town' = G6a (capital, 4-tier hierarchy, administrators, territorial expansion per Spencer 2010) and G6b (records and writing, Shin et al. 2020 information threshold) as separate triggers that may occur in either order. About 150-500 years.

An alternative 3-act split follows Flannery & Marcus's three transitions: (I) egalitarian village to achievement-based society, (II) to hereditary rank/chiefdom, (III) to state.

Equivalents of the user's Near Eastern anchors in other regions: Ubaid-type chiefdoms correspond to China mid-Yangshao to Longshan, Egypt Naqada I-II and Oaxaca San José to Rosario. Uruk (c. 5300 BP / 3300 BCE) corresponds to Egypt Dynasty 0-1, China Erlitou (+ Shang writing) and Oaxaca Monte Albán Late I. Some items above (Fayum storage pits, collapse of the Varna/KGK VI horizon after c. 4200 BCE, Graeber & Wengrow-style critiques of stage models) are general background knowledge and were not verified in this search. Treat them as such.

parts.real_world: 西アジア: 後期銅石器〜後期ウルク (前 4,200〜3,100 年ごろ)。ほかの地域: エジプト第 0〜1 王朝 (前 3,200〜3,000 年ごろ。アビドス U-j の文字 前 3,320〜3,150 年ごろ)、中国の二里頭 (前 1,750〜1,530 年ごろ) と殷の甲骨文字 (前 1,250 年ごろ)、オアハカのモンテ・アルバン (国は前 300〜100 年ごろ、文字は前 600 年ごろ)
parts.theory_basis: Service・Fried・Johnson & Earle の「国」。Wright & Johnson 1975 (3 段以上の行政)。Spencer 2010 (国の仕組みと、1 日で行き来できない遠くへの広がりが一緒に出る)。Shin ほか 2020 (規模のしきいと情報のしきいは別)。国と文字の順番は地域で逆になる
sources: Spencer 2010, PNAS 107:7119-7126: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2867764
Shin et al. 2020, Nature Communications 11:2394
Wright & Johnson 1975, American Anthropologist 77(2)
Dee et al. 2013, Proc. R. Soc. A 469:20130395 (エジプトの年代)
Liu & Xu 2007, Antiquity 81 (二里頭)
Borcan, Olsson & Putterman 2021, Explorations in Economic History 82

pros: 地域をこえてくり返し見られる切れ目 (平等な村 → 受けつぐ差と首長 → 国) に合う
「差」と「首長」を同じ部に入れるので、どちらが先かという順番の問題 (下の phase_order_issues) を部の中で扱える
Flannery & Marcus の「3 つの移り変わり」という、はっきりした理論の裏づけがある
cons: 第1部が G1〜G3 で、G3 がまだ途中なので、いま区切りの報告ができない
第1部が約 7,000 年・3 フェーズで、まだ大きい
西アジアでは家ごとの倉 (G4 の前半) が PPNB (前 8,800〜6,900 年ごろ) に始まるので、G4 を「平等な村」のあとに置くのはずれる
段階をはしご (順番に必ず上る) とみる考えには批判が強い (Feinman & Neitzel 1984; Yoffee 2005; Graeber & Wengrow 2021)
ほかの地域の例が多く、西アジアの村の話としてはわかりにくい

synthesis.recommended:
案B (4部) をすすめます。

理由:
(1) G1・G2 は済んでいるので、第1部「村と畑」をいま閉じて、区切りの評価と動画を作れます。
(2) どの部も 1〜2 フェーズで、考古学の時期 (先土器新石器 / 土器新石器〜ハラフ / ウバイド / ウルク) と一対一になり、通説として説明しやすいです。調べた 4 つの見方のうち 3 つが、ほぼ同じ切れ目 (前 6,950〜6,650 年ごろの PPNC の分散、前 6,200〜5,500 年ごろ、前 4,200 年ごろ) をあげています。
(3) いま進行中の G3 と次の G4 が、「土器・印章・家の倉」の時代 (サビ・アビヤド、ハラフ) としてひとまとまりになります。
(4) チャイルドの 2 つの革命 (案A) は、第1部と第4部として残ります。
案A は第2部が G3〜G5 の 3 フェーズで、「大きすぎる」がそのまま残ります。案C は G3 が終わるまで第1部が閉じません。

あわせて相談したいこと:
G4 の「差」の条件 (ジニ係数 0.3 以上) は、ハラフ期の証拠 (豊かさの差が小さい) と合いません。そこで、第2部の G4 は「家の倉・持ち主・受けつぎ」を中心にします。大きな差 (高いジニ係数) は、第3部の終わり〜第4部 (ウバイド後期〜ウルク、前 4,000 年ごろの犂と牛) の目安に移す案です (Bogaard ほか 2019; Kohler ほか 2025)。

途中経過 (部の中の目安) の案:
- 第2部「土器と家の倉」
  - G3-1 土器を作りはじめる (前 7,000 年ごろ。最初はめずらしい品)
  - G3-2 毎日使う土器・鎌 (前 6,700 年ごろから)
  - G3-3 作る人が出る (いまの G3 の条件)
  - G4a 家の倉 (Flannery 2002 の段階 2)
  - G4b 受けつぎと持ち主の印 (サビ・アビヤドの印章 前 6,200 年ごろ)
- 第3部「まとめ役と神殿」
  - G5a 話し合い・長老・祭りでまとまる (Johnson 1982 の「順番の階層」。まとめ役がいなくても大きな共同作業はできた: ギョベクリ・テペ)
  - G5b 決まったまとめ役・罰・裁き (「同時の階層」。テル・アバダの首長の家)
- 第4部「町と文字」
  - G6a 村どうしの交換と町 (テル・ブラク 前 4,200 年ごろ)
  - G6b 記録 (トークン → 封筒 → 粘土板 → 文字、前 3,700〜3,200 年ごろ)
  - 町と文字は地域によって順番が逆になるので、別々の条件にします。
- 数で見える目安:
  - 村の大きさ 約 60 → 約 300 → 約 700 人 (Kuijt 2000 のまた聞きで、のちに下方修正。ゲームでは人口を現実の 1/10〜1/100 に縮めているので、その割合にします)
  - 家族が 6 つをこえると新しい決め方が要る (Johnson 1982)
  - 家の倉と村の蓄えの割合
  - 印・トークンを使っているか
  - 集落の段の数 1→2→3→4
  - 家の持ち物のジニ係数

時間の配分について: 通説では村の時代がいちばん長く、首長が出てから国になるまでは 500〜1,500 年ほどと速いです。部ごとのゲーム内の年数は同じにしないほうが現実に近くなります。また、PPNB の大きな村がばらけたように、止まる・後もどりすることも起きてよい結果として扱うと、通説に合います。
phase_order_issues: G3 の例「ウバイド期」がずれている: 上メソポタミアの土器は前 7,000〜6,700 年ごろに始まり (Leiden 'Relentlessly Plain'; Nieuwenhuyse ed. 2018)、ウバイドより 500〜1,500 年早い。最初の土器はめずらしい、交換で来る品で、毎日使う粗い土器は前 6,700 年ごろから。ウバイドは G5 (首長と神殿) の例にあたる。
土器は畑より約 2,500 年あと (西アジアの『先土器新石器』)。G2 → G3 の順番自体は西アジアでは正しい。ただし中国・メソアメリカ・エジプトでは、土器は最初の村と一緒に出るので、土器は『余りと分業』の目印としては西アジアでしか使えない (地域比較)。
分業に余りが要るとはかぎらない: PPNA・PPNB にはすでに作る人がいた (シュバイカ 6 のビーズ、ナヴィフォームの石刃、バジャの砂岩の輪、石灰しっくい)。階層のない社会で、余りとの結びつきもはっきりしない (Barzilai; Kuijt 2000)。Halstead 1989 の『ふつうの余り』では、余りは不作への備えで、自動的に作る人を養うわけではない。
貯蔵は家畜化より前: ドゥラーの倉は約 11,300〜11,175 年前で、作物が家畜化されるより約 1,000 年早い (Kuijt & Finlayson 2009 PNAS)。G3 の『余りをためる』は G2 より前から始まっている。
G4 の『家の持ち物』は G3 より前に始まる: 丸い家と共同の倉 → 四角い家と家ごとの倉への変化は PPNB (前 8,800〜7,500 年ごろ) で、土器より 1,500〜2,000 年早い (Flannery 2002; Byrd 1994)。

G4 の『差』が早すぎる: 豊かさの差は畑を始めてから少なくとも 4,000 年ほど小さいままで、前 4,000 年ごろの犂と牛 (土地で決まる農業) で大きくなる (Bogaard, Fochesato & Bowles 2019; Kohler ほか 2025 PNAS)。チャタルヒュユクは家の大きさがほぼ同じで、ウバイドも墓の差が小さい (Kopanias & Barlagianni)。Fried の順番でも、ランク (首長) が先で、経済の差 (階層化) があと。いまの『G4 差 → G5 リーダー』は、『差』の部分で通説と逆。
G4 の例 Kohler ほか 2017 とヴァルナは、遅い時期の例: ヴァルナ (前 4,596〜4,341 年ごろ) はバルカンの銅器時代で、西アジアではない。犂と結びつく後半の差 (G4b) の比べる例としてだけ使える (Higham ほか 2007/2018)。

G5 の『まとめ役がいないと大きな共同作業はできない』は早い時期の証拠と合わない: ギョベクリ・テペ (前 9,600〜8,200 年ごろ)、ジェリコの塔、ヒラゾン・タクティトの祭り (約 12,000 年前) は、目に見えるまとめ役なしに祭りと儀礼で行われた。規模のストレスはナトゥーフ期 (G1) から始まっていて、答え方には (1) 話し合いと祭り、(2) 決まった役、(3) 村が分かれる、の 3 つがある (Johnson 1982; Kuijt 2000; Watkins 2023)。
G5 の例『ウバイドの首長制』は主流だが、異論がある: Stein 1994 は首長制とみる。一方で墓の差はほとんどない (Kopanias & Barlagianni)、『平等の考え方』が表に出ていた (Graeber & Wengrow 2021) という見方もある。G5 の条件に目に見える豊かさの差を入れないほうがよい。

G6 は別々のものを 1 つにまとめている: 村どうしの交換は最初の村からある (黒曜石、ハラフの土器の交換 前 6,000 年ごろ)。記録の道具は早い (トークン 前 8,000/7,500 年ごろ〜、サビ・アビヤドの印章 前 6,200 年ごろ)。町 (テル・ブラク 前 4,200 年ごろ) は文字 (前 3,350〜3,200 年ごろ) より先。地域比較では国と文字の順番は逆にもなる (中国は国が先、オアハカは文字が先)。交換は G1 からの続く量、町と記録は別々の条件にするのが合う (Oates ほか 2007; Schmandt-Besserat; Spencer 2010; Shin ほか 2020)。
G1 の『定住で子が増える』: Bocquet-Appel 2011 は、出生の増加を畑を始めたこと (G2) と結びつけている。定住だけではない。南レヴァントでは PPNB の増え方が弱かったという研究もある。
通説の順番は一直線ではない: PPNB の大きな村は PPNC でばらけた (Kuijt 2000; Zielhofer ほか 2012)。ヨーロッパの LBK は人口が増えたあとに減った (Shennan ほか 2013)。ヴァルナやトリポリエの巨大集落は国にならなかった。止まる・後もどりする結果も起きてよい。
G2 の例ガンジ・ダレは、いちばん古い家畜の世話ではない: いちばんはっきりした、若いオスを選んでつぶした証拠 (約 1 万年前)。動物の世話は約 11,500 年前から (Zeder 2011)。

checks.claim: 1. ハラフの較正年代 約 前 5,900〜5,300 年
checks.correction: 中心の年代としては正しい。サビ・アビヤドの報告ではハラフの始まりは約 前 5,900〜5,400 年 (較正)、その前の移行期 (プロト・ハラフ) は 前 6,100〜5,900 年。カヴィ・タルラスの研究計画は北メソポタミアのハラフを 前 6,000〜5,300 年とする。ハラフからウバイドへの移行は 前 5,300〜5,200 年ごろ (テル・タウィーラ)。『前 6,100〜5,100』は移行期を前後に含めた幅。『前 6,500〜5,500』は古いか、移行期を混ぜた数で、使わないほうがよい。Akkermans の『前 5,200〜4,500』は較正していない年代。

checks.claim: 2. サビ・アビヤドの印章・封泥・倉: 前 6,200〜6,000 年 (Leiden) か 前 5,700〜5,000 年か
checks.correction: 本当の食い違いではない。前 6,200 年ごろ (較正) に大きな倉・トロス・印章・封泥が現れ、『焼けた村』(第 6 建築層) は 前 6,000 年ごろの火事で焼けた。『前 5,700〜5,000 年』は Akkermans & Duistermaat が使った較正前の年代で、同じ論文で較正すると 前 6,500〜5,800 年にあたると書いている。計画では較正した 前 6,200〜6,000 年に統一する。トークンが帳簿用だったかは議論がある (Bennison-Chapman)。

checks.claim: 3. ウバイド: 前 6,500〜3,800 年 (Carter & Philip 2010) と 前 5,500〜4,000 年 (Met)、ウバイド 0 は前 7 千年紀か 前 5,500〜5,400 年か
checks.correction: 『前 6,500〜3,800 年』は Carter & Philip 2010 の 2 ページ (『南のウバイドはウバイド 0 と 5 を含めて約 3,000 年』) に由来するとされる。ただし確認できたのはウィキペディアと Pleiades を通したまた聞きだけ。Met の 前 5,500〜4,000 年は北まで広がった時期のまとめで、Met 自身も南での始まりを 前 6,200 年ごろとしている。ウバイド 0 (ウェイリ) は CNRS によると前 7 千年紀で、ほかの資料では 前 6,500〜5,400 年。『ウバイド 0 = 前 5,500〜5,400 年』は誤りで、5,400 年はウバイド 0 の終わり (ウバイド 1 の始まり) にあたる。北のウバイドは 前 5,300〜4,300 年ごろ。

checks.claim: 4. Johnson 1982 の『家族など 6 つほどで新しい決め方が要る』しきい
checks.correction: Johnson の『魔法の数 6』は、決めごとをする集まりのなかの単位の数についての話。6 ほどを超えるとストレスが急に (指数関数的に) 増え、集団が分かれるか、単位を組みなおすか、上の段を作る。順番の階層にも同時の階層にもあてはまるとされる。規模は『いちばん下の単位』の数で測り、その単位は核家族でも拡大家族でもよい。そのため『家族 6 つ』はおおまかな言い換え。対処のしかたも『新しい決め方』だけでなく、分かれることや単位を大きくすること (核家族 → 拡大家族) も含む。P6 の『まず順番の階層、次に同時の階層』という順序は計画側の解釈で、Johnson は順番の階層を同時の階層に代わる平等な仕組みとして示している。

checks.claim: 5. Kohler ほか 2017: 家の大きさのジニ係数 狩猟採集 約 0.17、園耕 約 0.27、農耕 約 0.35
checks.correction: WSU の記事はそれぞれの中央値を 0.17・0.27・0.35 としていて、論文 (Nature 551:619-622) とも一致する。論文の表では未確認。どれも家の大きさだけで測った値で、資産全体のジニ係数ではない。Kerig ほかの 2025 年 PNAS 論文は、技術が広まった前後で家の格差は大きく変わらないと反論している (ブログ経由の要約で確認)。

checks.claim: 6. Bogaard, Fochesato & Bowles 2019: 前 4,000 年ごろの犂と牛でジニ係数が約 2 倍
checks.correction: 『前 4,000 年ごろから格差が急に増える』と、『人手で決まる農業から土地で決まる農業へ変わると、大きく長く続く格差が出る』は確認できた (90 の遺跡の時期、Antiquity 93)。牛に犂をひかせることを中心に置いたのは主に報道の書き方で、論文の要旨は『土地で決まる農業』として書いている。『約 2 倍』の数字は資料で確認できなかった。

checks.claim: 7. Kohler, Bogaard ほか 2025 PNAS: 長く続く豊かさの差は畑を始めてから 1,000 年以上あと
checks.correction: 要旨に『長く続く豊かさの差は、ふつう畑を始めてから 1,000 年以上遅れて現れる』とある。WSU の発表は約 1,500 年としている。人口の増加、土地の不足、集落の段が増えることと結びつけていて (1,100 以上の遺跡、47,000 以上の家)、P9 の『集落の段と一緒に出る』とも合う。DOI 10.1073/pnas.2400691122。

checks.claim: 8. Flannery & Marcus 2012: 西アジアで受けつぐ身分が約 7,500 年前
checks.correction: 本の抜粋に、西アジアの受けつぐエリートは約 7,500 年前、ペルーは約 4,000 年前、メキシコは約 3,000 年前とある (Montreal Review 経由で確認、ページ数は未確認)。約 7,500 年前は 前 5,500 年ごろで、サマッラ後期からウバイド前期にあたる。

checks.claim: 9. 上メソポタミアの土器 前 7,000〜6,700 年ごろ、毎日使う粗い土器は 前 6,700 年ごろから (サビ・アビヤド)
checks.correction: 前 7,000〜6,700 年 (較正) は『初期土器新石器』で、鉱物を混ぜたよく作られた少数の器 (Early Mineral Ware)。そのあと約 300 年して、植物を混ぜた粗い『Standard Ware』が多くなる。ただ、最初の土器は『よそから来た』だけではない。多くの遺跡でよそから来た器と地元で作った器が一緒に見つかり、どこで生まれたかはまだわからない。

checks.claim: 10. PPNC のアイン・ガザル 約 8,900〜8,600 年前、PPNB 後期の大きな村の人口 (1,500〜4,000 人か数百人か)
checks.correction: PPNC を 8.9〜8.6 千年前 (較正) とするのは、Rollefson が共著の 2012 年の研究のとおり。前 6,950〜6,650 年ごろにあたる。PPNC 全体は前 6,400 年ごろまでとする資料もある。人口ははっきりしない。ウィキペディアなどは最盛期 (前 7,000 年ごろ、10〜15 ha) を約 2,500〜3,000 人とし、Rollefson は PPNB 中期を 700〜900 人として、それが数世代で倍になったという。最近は、同じ時期に建っていた家を数えすぎているとして、アイン・ガザルなどを『数千人ではなく数百人』とみる意見がある (Kuijt ほか)。計画では『数百〜3,000 人ほど、議論あり』とするのが安全。

checks.claim: 11. Kuijt 2000 の村の人口 (約 60、330、765、3,000〜4,000 人) と、のちに本人が下方修正したこと
checks.correction: 60・330・765・3,000〜4,000 という数そのものは、原論文 (JAA 19) を開けず確認できなかった。下方修正のほうは確かめられた。Kuijt は Marciniak と 2024 年にチャタルヒュユクを 600〜800 人とし (以前の推定は 2,800〜10,000 人)、2025 年の講演では西アジア新石器の集落の人口推定全体がふくらみすぎていると論じている。ただ、2000 年の数字そのものを本人が直したかどうかは未確認。

checks.claim: 12. テル・ブラク: LC2 約 55 ha・LC3 約 130 ha (Ur) と『ほぼ 300 ha』
checks.correction: Ur によると LC2 (前 4,200〜3,800 年) は中心の丘と周りの小さな集落を合わせて約 55 ha。約 130 ha は LC3〜4 (前 3,800〜3,400 年) のほぼつながった輪の形の集落 (Ur, Karsgaard & Oates 2007 Science も 130 ha)。ウィキペディアは 130 ha を Period F (LC3) とする。ブラクを『ほぼ 300 ha』とする根拠は見つからなかった。近くのハムーカルの南の広がり (LC1〜2、約 280〜300 ha の黒曜石の散らばり) とまざった可能性が高い。

checks.claim: 13. ウルクの大きさ (80、100、250 ha) と人口 (4〜8 万人)
checks.correction: 数のちがいは時期と測り方のちがい。後期ウルクの約 250 ha がいちばん多く引かれる。約 100 ha は Van De Mieroop の『前 3,200 年ごろ』の推定か、ウルク前期の値。約 80 ha の根拠は見つからなかった。人口 4 万人は 1 ha あたり約 160 人とした計算で、1 ha あたり 100〜300 人なら 2.5〜7.5 万人。5〜8 万人は前 2,900 年ごろの城壁内 (約 6 km²) の値で、後期ウルクではない。人口の数はおもに一般向けの資料にしかない。

checks.claim: 14. 原楔形文字 (ウルク IV) 前 3,350〜3,200 年、数の粘土板 前 3,500〜3,350 年、トークン入りの封筒 前 3,700〜3,500 年
checks.correction: ウルク IV = 前 3,350〜3,200 年と、数だけの粘土板 = ウルク V (前 3,500〜3,350 年) は標準の区分どおり。数の粘土板はブラク、ハブーバ・カビーラ、ジェベル・アルーダでも出る。封筒 (ブッラ) は『いちばん古いものは前 4 千年紀の中ごろ (ウルク VI/V)』とされ、前 3,700 年は早すぎる。前 3,500 年前後とし、数の粘土板とほぼ同じ時期に重なると書くほうが正確。

checks.claim: 15. いちばん古いトークン (ガンジ・ダレ/テペ・アシアブの前 8,000/7,500 年か、ムレイベトの前 9,000〜8,700 年か)
checks.correction: Schmandt-Besserat はトークンの始まりを前 8,000 年ごろ (別の文では前 7,500 年ごろ) とし、テペ・アシアブを約 前 7,800 年とする。ガンジ・ダレもムレイベトもトークンの出る遺跡に挙げているが、遺跡ごとの年代は確認できなかった。彼女の年代はたいてい較正していない古い年代なので、較正すると古くなる。ムレイベトの前 9,000〜8,700 年が較正した値なら、食い違いの多くは較正の有無で説明できる (推測)。最初期の小さな粘土の玉が数を数える道具だったかは議論がある (Bennison-Chapman)。

checks.claim: 16. ドゥラーの倉 約 11,300〜11,175 年前 (Kuijt & Finlayson 2009)
checks.correction: 要旨どおり (約 11,300〜11,175 cal BP、PNAS 2009)。前 9,350〜9,225 年ごろにあたる。床を浮かせた倉で、植物の加工場のあいだにあり、作物の家畜化 (栽培化) より 1,000 年以上前。

checks.claim: 17. ガンジ・ダレのヤギ 約 1 万年前と、動物の世話の始まり 約 11,500 年前 (Zeder 2011)
checks.correction: ガンジ・ダレの集落は約 1 万年前で、ヤギの群れの管理は約 9,900 BP (Zeder & Hesse)。Zeder 2011 (Current Anthropology 52 S4) の要旨は、のちの家畜と作物の『形の変わらない野生のものの管理』が『少なくとも 11,500 cal BP、たぶんもっと前』に始まるとする。この 11,500 年前は動物と植物の両方についての値で、ヤギだけの値ではない。

checks.claim: 18. ナトゥーフ期の始まり 約 15,000/14,600 年前、ヤンガードリアス 約 12,900〜11,700 年前
checks.correction: ナトゥーフ前期の始まりは資料により約 15,000〜14,500 cal BP (シュバイカ 1 は 14,600 年前から)。ヤンガードリアスの 12,900〜11,700 年前は標準の値で、ナトゥーフ後期と重なる。

checks.claim: 19. ギョベクリ・テペ 前 9,600〜8,200 年 (古い木の影響で見なおし)
checks.correction: 前 9,600〜8,200 年 (PPNA〜PPNB 前期) はよく引かれる値。終わりは DAI が PPNB 中期のあと (前 8,000 年ごろ) とし、もっと遅くまで続いたとする資料もある。年代の問題は『古い木』というより、埋め土に古いものが入ること (埋め土の年代は『それより前』の目安にしかならない) と、土の炭酸塩の年代の問題。壁のしっくいの炭で囲い D は 前 9,745〜9,314 年。『古い木で見なおし』とはっきり書いた資料は見つからなかった。
要旨どおり (Radiocarbon 60(2):493-516、95.4%)。始まり 前 4,596〜4,516 年、終わり 前 4,427〜4,341 年、続いたのは約 120〜260 年。『前 4,590〜4,340 年』は別の論文 (Documenta Praehistorica 44) の値。

checks.claim: 21. Bocquet-Appel 2011: 女の人 1 人あたり子が約 2 人増える、500〜700 年の信号
checks.correction: 『合計特殊出生率が約 2 人増える』は 2011 年の Science (333:560-561) の要旨どおり。『500〜700 年』は 2002 年のヨーロッパ・北アフリカの墓地の研究 (子どもの骨の割合が 500〜700 年で 20〜30% 増える) の値で、2011 年の論文の値ではない。北アメリカでは 600〜800 年。

checks.claim: 22. Frangipane 2007: ハラフ = 水平な平等、サマッラ・ウバイド = 垂直な平等
checks.correction: 要旨 (World Archaeology 39(2):151-176) は、上下のない『水平な平等』と、特別な地位と大まかな平等が両立する『垂直な平等』を分け、北のハラフと中部・南のサマッラ・ウバイドを比べている。どちらがどちらかは要旨の書き方と、よく引かれる読み方からの判断で、本文は未確認。

checks.claim: 23. 『行政の段が 3 つ以上・集落が 4 段で国』の出どころは Wright 1977 か Johnson 1982/1987 か
checks.correction: もとは Wright & Johnson 1975 (American Anthropologist 77:267-289) の『国 = 専門の行政があり、決める段が少なくとも 3 つある社会』という定義。Johnson 1973 (国の操作上の定義、情報処理の必要)、Wright 1977 (首長制と国の段の数) がこれを補う。『集落 4 段』はそこから引き出した目安。Johnson 1982 は規模のストレスの論文で、出どころではない。3 段の文言は手元で直接は確認できず、記憶と要約による。

checks.claim: 24. シュバイカ 6 のビーズづくりの研究と、Willcox & Stordeur の Antiquity 論文の年 (2012 か 2014 か)
checks.correction: ビーズの研究は Thuesen, Alarashi, Ruter & Richter 2023 で、Antiquity ではなく PLOS ONE 18(12)。シュバイカ 6 の Antiquity 論文は Richter ほか 2016 の集落の報告。Willcox & Stordeur は 2012 (Antiquity 86(331):99-114、ジェルフ・エル・アフマルの大規模な穀物加工) で、2014 ではない。

checks.claim: 25. エジプトのナカダの各時期の年代 (Dee ほか 2013 にもとづく要約表)
checks.correction: 原論文の表 1 は開けなかった。要約によると、ナカダ期の始まり 前 3,800〜3,700 年、ナカダ IA〜IIB 前 3,800/3,750〜3,450 年、IIC〜D 前 3,450〜3,325 年、IID〜IIIA 前 3,377〜3,238 年 (2σ)、アハの即位 前 3,111〜3,045 年、バダリ 約 前 4,400〜3,800 年。Dee ほか 2014 は、細かい時期の単位ではナカダの相対編年は信頼が下がると注意している。

年代はどれも確認した値と合う (ナトゥーフ 15,000〜11,700 BP、ドゥラー 11,300 BP は PPNA のなか、ガンジ・ダレ 約 1 万年前 = 前 8,000 年、アイン・ガザル PPNC 8.9〜8.6 ka)。注意点は 3 つ。ガンジ・ダレはレヴァントではなくザグロス。PPNC を地域全体で前 6,400 年ごろまでとする資料もある。Flannery 2002 の段階 1 (丸い家と共同の倉) → 段階 2 (四角い家と家ごとの倉) は要旨と一致する。

checks.claim: P2. 第2部 土器と家と首長: 土器新石器 (前 7,000〜6,700) → ハッスーナ・サマッラ・ハラフ (前 6,500〜5,000) → ウバイド (南で前 6,200/5,500〜4,200)
checks.correction: 前半は正しい。ウバイドの終わりの 4,200 年は少数派で、Met は 4,000 年、Carter & Philip はウバイド 5 を含めて 3,800 年。テル・アバダの建物 A が特別なのは確か (いちばん大きく、壁に飾りがあり、乳児の埋葬の約半分がここにあり、トークンの多くもここで出て、16 個のトークンが入った鉢もある)。ただ『首長の家』は解釈で、資料で確かめられなかった。『名前のない間』はチャイルドの言葉ではなく計画側の言い方。Stein 1994 は『儀礼で主食を集め、仲間であることを強調するみんなのための考え方』で要旨と合う。

ブラク LC2 の約 55 ha、ウルク IV、Oates ほか 2007 (北は前 5 千年紀の終わりにはもう町に向かっていた)、Johnson 1973 (情報処理の必要) は確認できた。直すところは 2 つ。封筒は前 3,500 年前後が妥当で、前 3,700 年は早い。数の粘土板 (ウルク V、前 3,500〜3,350 年) は中期と後期の境にかかるので、『後期ウルク』の下に置くと少しずれる。Wright & Johnson 1975 は国の始まりをウルク前期 (前 4,000 年ごろ) に置いているので、スシアナの段の話は中期ウルクに限らない。

checks.claim: P4. 第1部 村と畑 (P1 と同じ年代、Kuijt 2000; Kadowaki 2012)
checks.correction: 年代は P1 と同じで問題ない。Kuijt 2000 は 8,500〜8,000 年前 (較正していない値とみられる) の大きな村の衰えと人口を論じていて、終わりを『大きな村の分散』とするのに合う。Kadowaki 2012 の中身は確認できなかった。

checks.claim: P5. 第2部 土器と家の倉: 土器新石器 → サビ・アビヤドの焼けた村 (前 6,200〜6,000) → ハッスーナ・サマッラ・ハラフ (前 6,500〜5,300)、チャタルヒュユク (前 7,100〜6,000)
checks.correction: 年代はおおむね正しい。チャタルヒュユク東の丘は、ベイズモデルで最古の層が前 7,100 年ごろ、終わりが前 6,000 年の少しあと (Bayliss ほか 2015、Marciniak ほか 2015)。UNESCO は 前 7,400〜6,200 年としている。『最初はよそから来る土器』は言いすぎで、多くの遺跡でよそから来た器と地元の器が一緒に出る。Flannery 2002 の段階 3 (15〜20 人の拡大家族) は要旨と一致する。Bogaard ほか 2009 (Antiquity『Private pantries and celebrated surplus』) と Halstead 1989 は検索で確認できず、記憶でのみ存在を確認。

checks.claim: P6. 第3部 まとめ役と神殿: ウバイド (南 前 6,200/5,500〜4,200、北 前 5,300〜4,300)、エリドゥ、テル・アバダ、テペ・ガウラ、デイルメンテペの封泥
checks.correction: 北のウバイド 前 5,300〜4,300 年、テペ・ガウラ XIII 層のアクロポリスの封泥 (中央でまとめる経済の可能性)、デイルメンテペの約 450 の封泥は確認できた。南の終わりの 4,200 年は P2 と同じ問題がある。テル・アバダの『首長の家』は解釈。Johnson の『順番の階層 → 同時の階層』という順序は計画側の解釈 (項目 4 を参照)。Carneiro 1981 と Blanton ほか 1996 は検索の上限で確認できず、記憶によるもの。

checks.claim: P7. 第4部 町と文字: ブラク LC2 (55 ha、LC3 で 130 ha) → 中期ウルク (スシアナの 4 段の集落、封筒 前 3,700〜3,500) → 後期ウルク (ウルク 100〜250 ha)
checks.correction: Ur は 130 ha を LC3〜4 (前 3,800〜3,400 年) としている。封筒は前 3,500 年前後に直す。『スシアナの 4 段』の段の数は確認できなかった。Wright & Johnson 1975 は前期ウルクの段を論じている。Shin ほか 2020 は Antiquity ではなく Nature Communications 11 で、『規模のしきい → 情報のしきい』の順は要旨と合う。Bogaard ほか 2019 の前 4,000 年ごろも確認できた。

checks.claim: P8. 第1部 平等な村: 西アジアのナトゥーフ〜ハラフ (前 13,000〜5,500)、裴李崗〜前期仰韶 (前 7,000〜4,000)、ティエラス・ラルガス (前 1,500〜1,150)、ファイユーム〜バダリ (前 5,400〜3,800)
checks.correction: ティエラス・ラルガスは 前 1,500〜1,150 年 (Marcus & Flannery、Seshat は 1,400 年から)。バダリは約 前 4,400〜3,800 年。直すところは 2 つ。(1) ハラフは前 5,300 年ごろまで続くので、5,500 年で切ると合わない。(2) サマッラ (前 6,200〜5,700 年ごろ) はハラフより前か同じころで、プロト・ハラフ (前 6,100〜5,900 年) にサマッラの影響がある。そのため『ナトゥーフ〜ハラフ = 平等、サマッラ以後 = 受けつぐ差』という分け方は年代が重なる。サビ・アビヤドの印章と倉 (前 6,200 年) もこの『平等』の期間に入る。『村から受けつぐ差まで 300〜3,000 年』は確認できなかった。

checks.claim: P9. 第2部 受けつぐ差と首長: サマッラ〜ウバイド (前 5,500〜4,000)、仰韶中期、ナカダ I〜IIB (前 3,750〜3,450)、サン・ホセ (前 1,150〜850)、ヴァルナ (前 4,600〜4,350)
checks.correction: Flannery & Marcus の約 7,500 年前、ナカダ IA〜IIB 前 3,800/3,750〜3,450 年 (Dee にもとづく要約)、サン・ホセ 前 1,150〜850 年 (Seshat)、ヴァルナ (Higham 2018)、Kohler 2025 は確認できた。ただしサマッラの始まりは前 5,500 年ではなく前 6,200 年ごろ。前 5,500 年から始めるなら『サマッラ後期〜ウバイド』か『ウバイド (0〜4)』と呼ぶほうが正確。

checks.claim: P10. 第3部 町と国と文字: 後期銅石器〜後期ウルク (前 4,200〜3,100)、エジプト第 0〜1 王朝 (アビドス U-j 前 3,320〜3,150)、二里頭 (前 1,750〜1,530)、甲骨文字 (前 1,250)、モンテ・アルバン (国 前 300〜100、文字 前 600)
checks.correction: 二里頭 前 1,750〜1,530 年 (2007 年の炭素年代)、武丁期の甲骨 前 1,254〜1,197 年、アハの即位 前 3,111〜3,045 年、モンテ・アルバン後期 I (前 300〜100 年) で国ができた (Spencer & Redmond) は確認できた。U-j の 前 3,320〜3,150 年は二次資料で、ナカダ IIIA1 か IIIA2 かも分かれている (約 前 3,300 年)。サン・ホセ・モゴテ記念物 3 の『前 600 年』は議論があり、前 200 年かもっと後とする説もある。Spencer 2010 PNAS (1 日で行き来できる範囲を超える広がり) は検索の上限で確認できなかった。国と文字の順番が地域で逆になる (エジプトとオアハカは文字が先、中国は国が先) は上の年代と合う。

verification.summary:
25 の主張のうち、そのまま使えるのは 8 つ (1、5、7、8、9、16〜18、20、22 のうちの主なもの)。残りはほとんどが一部だけ正しいもので、はっきりした誤りは数か所。年代の食い違いの多くは、較正した年代と較正していない古い年代がまざっていることで説明できる (サビ・アビヤドの『前 5,700〜5,000 年』、たぶんトークンの年代、Akkermans のハラフの年代)。

**直す必要があるところ**
- **ブラクの『ほぼ 300 ha』**: 根拠が見つからない。近くのハムーカルの約 280〜300 ha とまざった可能性が高い。ブラクは LC2 で約 55 ha、LC3〜4 で約 130 ha (Ur)。
- **ウバイド 0 = 前 5,500〜5,400 年**: 誤り。ウバイド 0 は前 7 千年紀で、5,400 年はその終わりにあたる。
- **シュバイカ 6 のビーズの研究**: Antiquity ではなく PLOS ONE (Thuesen ほか 2023)。Willcox & Stordeur は 2012 年。
- **Shin ほか 2020**: 掲載誌は Nature Communications。
- **国の定義『3 段以上』の出どころ**: Wright & Johnson 1975 (Johnson 1973 と Wright 1977 が補う)。Johnson 1982 ではない。
- **Bocquet-Appel の『500〜700 年』**: 2011 年ではなく 2002 年の研究の値。
- **トークン入りの封筒**: 前 3,700 年は早すぎ、前 3,500 年前後が妥当。
- **区切りの年代のずれ**: サマッラの始まりは前 6,200 年ごろで、P9 の『前 5,500 年から』と P8 の『ハラフまで = 平等』の区切りと重なる。ハラフは前 5,300 年ごろまで続く。

**確認できなかったもの**
- Bogaard 2019 の『ジニ係数が約 2 倍』
- Kuijt 2000 の人口の数そのもの
- 原論文の表にあるナカダの細かい年代

**途中の区切りに使える、年代が確かな目印**
- ナトゥーフ (15,000〜11,700 BP)
- ドゥラーの倉 (11,300 BP)
- 動物と植物の世話の始まり (11,500 cal BP 以前)
- PPNC の分散 (8,900〜8,600 BP)
- 上メソポタミアの土器 (前 7,000〜6,700 年)
- サビ・アビヤドの倉と印章 (前 6,200〜6,000 年)
- ハラフ (前 5,900〜5,300 年)
- 受けつぐ身分 (約 7,500 年前)
- ブラク LC2 (前 4,200〜3,800 年)
- 前 4,000 年ごろの土地で決まる農業
- ウルク V/IV (前 3,500〜3,200 年)
